newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-BRAZIL UNVEIL NEW KIT AND DEAL WITH NIKE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRAZIL UNVEIL NEW KIT AND DEAL WITH NIKE.

text.p: Brazil unveiled a new kit for their national soccer team on Thursday as part of a ten-year multi-million dollar contract with sports manufacturers Nike.

Nike have added a thick green stripe down the sleeves of the famous gold shirt in one of the most dramatic changes ever made to the Brazilian kit. The stripe got a mixed reaction from journalists present at the unveiling.
The national team shirt is a hugely sensitive matter amongst Brazilians and is treated almost as a matter of national security.

In 1987, a soft drinks company sponsoring the team caused an outcry by emblazening a huge red emblem on the front of the shirt. Critics likened the move to putting the sponsor's name on the national flag. It was subsequently removed after just one game.
Ricardo Teixeira, president of the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF), said Nike would provide a variety of investments in addition to the team strip.

These included the organisation of a championship between shanty towns, the creation of a Brazilian soccer museum and the construction of a new headquarters to replace the decaying eight-storey building in central Rio which currently houses the CBF.
"This is more than just a partnership, it is an association," Teixeira said.
It was not revealed how much Nike were paying in sponsorship money but reports suggested the deal was worth well over one hundred million dollars over ten years.
